explanation: Each of the harp's seven pedals sets every string of one note name, such as all the Cs, to flat, natural or sharp. Most modern pianos have three pedals.

claims.text: A modern concert (pedal) harp has seven pedals.
A modern piano, grand or upright, usually has three pedals.
Each harp pedal sets all the strings of one note name to flat, natural or sharp.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic02w. Claims: every checkable statement in the labels, values and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers instruments, so both counts need web evidence from the checkers. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for 'b': most players picture a harp with no pedals at all, which is the trap. Argued against the key: a pedal harp has seven pedals, one per note name; a modern piano has three (some uprights and older grands two), so the answer holds either way. Counterintuitive is true, so both label claims are high under C26. Exact counts, so the 1.1 times guard does not apply. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: both instruments are the same everywhere. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: None. b01's piano and harp item compares strings, and the guide's e.0007 example counts a harp's strings; this item counts pedals.
